participants: Andrew Musial (closer, appears in diarization as 'Andrew Jin (Primal Instinct)')
summary: Twenty-six-minute manager 1-1, opened with an explicit recording disclosure. Andrew reported an error on a deal he had just closed: he sold a three-payment plan of $2,000 each with no interest applied, which Chris confirmed is not the intended structure — payment plans are supposed to carry interest. Chris chose to honour the terms as sold and proposed converting the mistake into a referral ask, timed immediately so the concession would still feel live. Numbers were reviewed briefly: four deals month to date against a live-call close rate of about 26.6%, which Chris said is in Andrew's normal 28-30% band. The operational theme was show rate — Andrew is drowning in follow-ups because no-shows are the majority of his unconverted pipeline, Kim is the only setter and cannot keep up with lead volume, and Derek Harris is being brought on to dial from Thursday or Friday. Andrew described a personal system in which he keeps a Google Sheet of everyone he has closed and connects it to Claude to be told what to do with each client. The back half of the call was a long personal conversation about detachment from money, sitting with emotion, and consciousness, prompted by Andrew asking how to stay neutral on days he does not close.
notable: Stated payment-plan policy: interest is supposed to be applied. Chris, on Andrew's 3x$2,000 close — 'I wasn't supposed to just have you do it for 2K for three months, like there is supposed to be typically a bit of interest on that.' The total ($6,000) is on-price; the terms are not. Andrew's account: 'I just, like, in the motions, I never did it 3Pay, and I just totally forgot about it.' This is a benchmark for scoring payment plans in every other call in the corpus.

The company honours mis-sold terms rather than re-pricing: 'I'm not saying you have to pay any more. We're going to honor what we obviously said.' Immediately followed by the referral ask, with the timing chosen deliberately — Andrew suggested waiting a few weeks and Chris pushed back: 'I mean, it really should be now because otherwise the whole, like, angle of, like, we really weren't [supposed to].'

Deposits are taken and refunded in practice, corroborating the deposit move in objection play OB: 'I had this guy, who eventually we refunded him the deposit because he just been ghosting. But he got scared.' He was a medical resident.

No-shows are the dominant failure mode and they leave no recording. Andrew: 'they're piling up and they are piling up fast because there's a lot of people that are not showing up... no-shows are the majority of them.' He had confirmed one prospect by phone two hours before the call and still got stood up. Chris: 'Biggest priority for you right now that we need to focus on is just getting your show rate back up, more people showing up, need more live calls per day.'

Close-rate benchmark stated on the record: 'You're at four deals on the month divided by [live calls]... your live calls is about 26.6, which is right in that range of where you typically sit between like 28 to 30.' Any close rate computed from this corpus should be reconciled against that 28-30% band.

Setter capacity is the stated bottleneck. Chris: 'I was looking at how many leads he's getting assigned and everything, and he can't keep up with it. We were trying to have him be the only setter for a bit, but it's just so many leads coming in.' Derek Harris starts on dials Thursday or Friday and shadows Kim before Kim goes on holiday.

Client records are being processed through a personal Claude workflow outside company systems, with the manager's approval: 'I made a document, like a Google sheet, with all the guys that I closed, and with the dates that I need to remember about... and I connected it with Claude, and so on, so I just get into Claude and ask him, like, hey, what should I do with any of the prospects?' Chris: 'That's awesome. That's pretty sweet.' Andrew repeats the pattern at the end of the call with the transcript of the 1-1 itself.

Prospect profile intelligence consistent with the stated ICP: a fourth-year surgical resident (no-showed) and an anaesthesiology resident in New York (deposit refunded after ghosting). Chris noted the resident 'is still working off his debt. He's not getting his full salary thing yet' — an income-screening nuance the ICP criteria do not capture.
Recording disclosure was given at the top of the call — 'Yo. This meeting is being recorded.' Worth recording as the positive control against sales calls in this batch where no disclosure appears.
